A large platform whose systems miss terror content (392), calls for killings (393), threats of violence (419), bestiality themed images (229) or clips of a real death (366): the registered social media code requires the largest services to detect and remove pro-terror material and to enforce their rules against crime and violence material, which covers material that incites violence, shows bestiality, or shows real violence with a high impact. 129 counts for its violence and incitement part only. All of this applies only to material that would be refused classification; whether a clip of a suicide counts as real violence is not settled by the text. Left out: hate speech and racist abuse (163, 343, 143), eating disorder content (132), fraud ads (316) and misinformation (84, 213), which the code does not cover. The code took effect after every one of these incidents.

132: videos promoting eating disorders got past a large platform's detection by misspelled search terms; the code requires a service that bans self-harm material, which includes material promoting an eating disorder, to run systems that detect and remove it. 366: clips of a real suicide spread past the same kind of system; real images of violence or gore are high-impact violence material under the same duty.
